brief.headline: Close the 16.6% gap on our PET amber bottle by benchmarking to Suraj Blow Plast's ₹1.87/NOS and offer 15-day payment in return for a price cut near their 10.27% borrowing cost.

priceAsk.summary: Match Suraj Blow Plast's price on PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G
priceAsk.basis: Suraj Blow Plast delivers the same SKU at ₹1.87/NOS; the 16.6% gap is our entire excess spend estimate

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer 15-day payment (from current 30 days) in exchange for a ~10% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Accelerating payment frees ₹46539 of our working capital, but paying 15 days early is worth roughly their 10.27% borrowing cost to them — use it as a swap for part of the price gap

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is financially stable but operationally stretched. Their 3.8% net margin matches the peer median of 3.7%, yet their 7.6% return on capital lags the peer 13.4%, signalling inefficiency. They hold an [ICRA] A / Stable rating and low 0.19x debt-to-equity with 4.55x interest coverage, so continuity risk is minimal. However, their Altman Z-score of 2.77 sits in the grey zone, GST and EPF filing delays hint at administrative stress, and their Probe42 score is a weak 4/10. We represent only 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue, giving us negligible standalone leverage — we must compete them against alternates and bundle any commitment to earn a discount.

evidence.point: Our PET amber bottle costs 16.6% more than the best price we pay elsewhere
TPAC's return on capital is nearly half the peer median, suggesting operational inefficiency
evidence.figure: 7.6% return on capital vs peer median 13.4%

evidence.point: Their effective borrowing cost makes early payment valuable to them
Their Altman Z sits in the distress grey zone despite the A rating
We are a tiny customer with negligible revenue share
evidence.figure: ₹11.32 L spend = 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Administrative stress visible in compliance delays
evidence.figure: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, covers pharma bottles, caps, and preforms — a credible, scaled second source with B (65/100) health

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue) serving pharma with strong A (79/100) health; robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle/jar specialist (Pearlpet brand, ₹19.83 Cr revenue) — direct fit for our PET amber bottle SKU, though weaker D (32/100) health

risks: TPAC's grey-zone Altman Z (2.77) and compliance delays mean pushing too hard on price may tip a fragile supplier — frame any squeeze around locking volume and qualifying a second source, not just cost
At 0.02% of their revenue we have almost no pull in isolation — any meaningful concession requires bundling SKUs, committing volume, or live competition from Manjushree or Mold-Tek
Their 17-day payable cycle vs peer 33d shows they already pay suppliers fast; they may resist further payment acceleration unless we offer a clear price trade
GST and EPF delays flag administrative strain — confirm on-time delivery track record and build a qualified backup before relying solely on TPAC for continuity
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the gap to Suraj Blow Plast's ₹1.87 on our PET amber bottle — can we discuss matching that price if we accelerate payment to 15 days, which saves you roughly your 10.27% borrowing cost?
